decisions.reason: A rye country bread is a low-cost staple on existing manual production lines, its value is still unresolved after one year, and keeping the option open costs little.
The premium raisin stollen has again won a gold medal from the Deutsches Brotinstitut and is a flagship product, so its value has largely been confirmed and justifies further commitment.
The seeded rye mixed bread has no negative signals and costs little to keep, though it overlaps with the firm's other rye breads, so it remains a cheap option worth holding.
The dark barley malt rye bread is a niche variant whose prospects are still uncertain, and with low carrying costs the firm should keep it while demand becomes clearer.

The marzipan stollen is a seasonal product that complements the award-winning stollen line and costs little to keep, so dropping it before more Christmas seasons have shown its value would be premature.
The ancient grain bread is presented as the newest masterpiece and fits the trend toward heritage grains, and its uncertain upside makes it worth keeping open.
